item.title: Regarding SCP-108 (and 336)
item.content:encoded:
So I noticed this tale briefly mentions an "SCP-108" that doesn't really match up with what currently holds that slot. I found this interesting because of all of the SCPs no longer on the list were -ARCs or -Ds and still allowed the reader to understand the context of what was happening.

However that is not the case with SCP-108-D.

Context and proposal underneath collapsible
Context and proposal

I had to take some time to actually find the damn thing, not only did I have to go on SCP Classic and look at the old EditThis SCPs, but I had to use the Wayback Machine to find an older version. This was bcause for some reason it seems it was here on the main site at some point, deleted, I assume through mod intervention.

The original SCP called "Man of War" depicted some super powerful guy, it's whatever and obviously don't hold up to the Wiki's current standards.

However I think "SCP-108-D" should be restored fully based on it just being mentioned in this tale.

I get that this tale hasn't aged well in some respects in the eyes of the community, but considering this is one of the biggest pieces of site history, one of the first tales that kickstarted and featured some of the old author avatars for the first time, and was one of the first big collabs. It deserves for its context to fully be intact for preservation purposes I feel.

With that said, I think we should bring back SCP-108-D for that reason.

(Also random side note, the SCP-336 in this tale doesn't match up with the current 336 rewrite and I believe the original version of 336 should also be archived similar to how the older version of 049 is archived. Not only that, but one of the more recent SCPs, SCP-4231, specifically makes reference of the older 336 so it may also be wise to restore it for other reasons as well.

item.title: Re: SCP-244, SCP-695
item.content:encoded:
To explain;nothing on the wiki is considered "canon". Each page, article, or Foundation tale is a seperate canon unto itself, though we strive for a certain degree of cohesion in regard to the actual articles. Thus, a Foundation tale needn't agree perfectly with an article or even be connected to any article at all.

That said, certain degrees of deviation from the source material are acceptable, and going beyond that threshold tends to result in downvotes and a quick deletion. A fanfic where 076-2 had one wing and weilded a laser sword in between drinking blood and attending orgies would probably not be tolerated. Nothing is canon, but some things just don't work.

item.title: Re: 122 paradox
item.content:encoded:
I think you're being far too picky about this. The main reason SCPs are decommissioned is because they are examples of what not to do. Otherwise, they are just reclassified as neutralised, or safe.

Although yes, we gave 122-d a death scene, that was more for our sake then anyone elses. Also to keep in mind, No one has set a date for anything. The Celf bruha could have occured at any time in the foundations history, wiping out 122-d with plenty of time for something else to be found.

Final conclusion: Fic-tion-al -char-ac-ters!
